 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Georgia stayed atop the latest College Football Playoff rankings, while surging Wake Forest moved up two spots and would be in the projected 12-team bracket if the postseason started this week.
 There was, as usual, a bit of movement among the top 10 in Tuesday night's bracket reveal, even though everyone on that list won last weekend.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement No. 8 Indiana and No. 9 Tennessee flip-flopped — a result that would give the Hoosiers home-field advantage in a projected first-round playoff game. Also, Texas moved to No. 5 on the strength of a win at LSU and it came at the expense of Notre Dame, which moved down to No. 6.
 Undefeated Utah was second, followed by Alabama with UCLA rounding out the coveted top four, all of which would receive first-round byes in the playoff.
 There are three more rankings to go, with the bracket set on Dec. 6, following a slate of conference title games.
 That could be the best opportunity for the first team out, 12th-ranked Texas Tech, to lock in its spot. The Red Raiders stayed put after a 25-point win over Oklahoma State, while Wake Forest moved up after a 49-7 stomping of SMU last week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Demon Deacons sport a 52-6 average winning margin over the last six games, the likes of which the selection committee purportedly does not consider in its evaluation.
 Rounding out the top 12 were Miami at No. 7 and BYU at No. 10, while Kentucky — the only top-12 team to lose last week — fell five spots to No. 16
